missionPremise: OPS-16 amendment A-073 (2026-09-02) added P-108 after two gaps surfaced while preparing the connector directory listing: a privacy policy with no retention section on a product about to take live money, and no documentation page while nine candidate routes serve the SPA shell. The card's governing constraint, and the reason it exists rather than being folded into P-88, is that retention must be described AS BUILT: terms.html previously promised a Stripe billing-portal cancellation path that existed nowhere in the app and it took a blocking card (A-062) to fix. An unenforced retention promise is the same defect wearing different clothes.
completionPredicate: A stranger can (a) reach a stable documentation URL that serves real HTML rather than the app shell, (b) read every sentence of the privacy retention section back to a store, a job, or a code path, and (c) run one command that FAILS when either stops being true. (a) is built and proven to the limit an uncommitted diff allows; (b) and (c) are met.
scopeBasis: The card names two gaps and bounds terms.html off because A-062 (PR #334) ships a check that reads it. Files touched are privacy.html, a new docs.html, vercel.json (the rewrite mechanism item 2 points at), a new guard and its self-test, the PE test script, the PE CI workflow, and one existing test whose expectation was wrong. Nothing in the dispatch's bounded-off list was touched. Excluded by the card and honoured: no directory-listing copy, no carousel images, no pricing/tier/capability change, no cookie banner or consent UI.

acceptanceItems.text: Retention is described as it actually is.
acceptanceItems.how: The store was read before the words were written. A new section, How long we keep things, states four things: what you can remove yourself, what stops working on its own, what is kept until you ask, and what account deletion actually does. Every sentence traces to a store, a job or a code path; the table is in CP2 under privacyRetentionProvenance. Three claims are deliberately NEGATIVE because that is what is true: nothing deletes on a schedule, the share grant row survives the link expiring, and account deletion does not reach saved properties or screens because no foreign key links them.

LESSON: A privacy or legal page is code-adjacent and rots the same way. The durable form of 'the page must stay true' is a guard that derives the number from the constant and the claim from the call site, not a review. Two of this guard's six checks are that shape and both fired correctly when the code and the page were pushed apart in opposite directions.

When a new guard fails on the real tree, interrogate the guard's INPUT before weakening its predicate. This one failed because an HTML source line wrapped mid-sentence. Weakening the sentence match to a keyword would have passed and would have destroyed the meaning-shaped property that made the check worth having.

Run a lexical screen's patterns against every file it will govern BEFORE wiring it in. Check 6 fired on '100%' in all three pages, from calc(100% - 40px) in inline CSS, because the prose normaliser stripped tags but not style bodies. Wiring first and then loosening the patterns would have narrowed a control to fit a defect in my own extractor.

An empty synthetic fixture makes a positive control fire and the case under test never runs. The guard caught its own test doing this: four-character stub pages tripped the blind-extractor floor, so the terms.html case asserted nothing. The fixture was lengthened; the floor was not lowered.

$? after a pipeline is the LAST command's status. The first violation battery read exit=0 on two cases the guard had correctly failed, because grep succeeded. DEV_PROCESS 2.3 names this and it still happened. Capture the real exit into a variable before any pipe.

The doc_repo concurrent-commit hazard fired during this lane: a parallel session's commit e42ac63 swept an uncommitted _catalog/seat_register.json edit made by THIS lane into ITS commit, so a commit describing P-109 also carries a P-108 worktree registration. Nothing was lost and nothing was corrupted, but a lane that assumes its doc_repo edits are still uncommitted at close will misreport. Re-check git log and git status for your own paths at close, not only at start.

It sits on feat/s1-instrument-hardening and is missing the share-grants route and eight pe_* schema files that exist on origin/main. An early grep for 'share-grants' returned nothing and would have supported a false absence. Read origin/main with git show; never the checkout.

Using the ORM source as the authority on cascade behaviour. The drizzle files declare onDelete cascade where an FK exists, but they cannot tell you that pe_saved_properties has no FK at all — that only shows up in information_schema against the live database. The catalog is the authoritative record; the schema file is a proxy for it.
